stem: Which of the following is a fundamental SI unit?
explanationCorrect: The kilogram is the SI base unit of mass. The others are derived from base units.

explanationsWrong.B: The newton is derived: 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻².
explanationsWrong.C: The joule is derived: 1 J = 1 N m.
explanationsWrong.D: The watt is derived: 1 W = 1 J s⁻¹.

stem: Which of these is a vector quantity?
explanationCorrect: Displacement has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector.

explanationsWrong.A: Speed has magnitude only; velocity is its vector form.

stem: A body starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of 2 m/s². How far does it travel in 5 s?

stem: A force acts on a 2 kg mass and gives it an acceleration of 3 m/s². What is the force?
explanationCorrect: Newton's second law: F = ma = 2 × 3 = 6 N.

stem: What is the weight of a 5 kg mass on Earth? (g = 10 m/s²)

explanationsWrong.A: 5 kg is the mass; weight is a force in newtons.

stem: Find the kinetic energy of a 2 kg body moving at 3 m/s.

explanationsWrong.A: 6 J is mv (momentum, in kg m/s), not energy.
explanationsWrong.D: 3 J squares nothing; v must be squared.

stem: A man lifts a 50 kg load through 4 m in 10 s. What is his power? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanationCorrect: Work = mgh = 50 × 10 × 4 = 2000 J. Power = work/time = 2000/10 = 200 W.

explanationsWrong.C: 2000 J is the work done, not power.
explanationsWrong.D: 500 N is the weight (mg); multiply by the height and divide by the time.

stem: A machine with velocity ratio 4 lifts a 600 N load with an effort of 200 N. What is its efficiency?

explanationsWrong.B: 133% inverts the ratio (VR/MA); real machines can't exceed 100%.
explanationsWrong.D: 300% is the MA expressed as a percentage.

stem: A spring of force constant 200 N/m is stretched by a force of 10 N. Find the extension.
explanationCorrect: Hooke's law: F = ke, so e = F/k = 10/200 = 0.05 m.

stem: Find the pressure due to water at a depth of 2 m. (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)

explanationsWrong.B: 200 Pa leaves out a factor of 100.

stem: A gas occupies 4 L at 100 kPa. At constant temperature it is compressed to 2 L. What is the new pressure?
explanationCorrect: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so P₂ = 100 × 4/2 = 200 kPa.

explanationsWrong.A: Halving the volume doubles the pressure; it doesn't halve it.
explanationsWrong.C: 400 kPa multiplies by 4 instead of by 4/2.
explanationsWrong.D: Pressure changes when volume changes at constant temperature.

explanationsWrong.A: 8400 J leaves out the temperature change.

Which describes the image formed by a plane mirror?
explanationCorrect: A plane mirror forms a virtual, upright image of the same size, laterally inverted (left and right swapped), as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

explanationsWrong.A: The image can't be caught on a screen, so it is virtual, not real.
explanationsWrong.C: It is upright and the same size, not inverted or magnified.
explanationsWrong.D: That describes a concave mirror with the object beyond C.

stem: A ray of light passes from air into glass with angle of incidence 60° and angle of refraction 30°. Find the refractive index of the glass.

explanationsWrong.B: 2.0 divides the angles (60/30), not their sines.
explanationsWrong.C: 0.58 is sin r / sin i — upside down.

stem: Which of these electromagnetic waves has the longest wavelength?
explanationCorrect: In order of increasing wavelength: gamma, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwaves, radio. Radio waves are longest.

explanationsWrong.B: Ultraviolet is shorter than visible light.
explanationsWrong.C: Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength.

stem: A 100 W lamp is used for 5 hours. How much energy does it use in kWh?
explanationCorrect: 100 W = 0.1 kW. Energy = 0.1 kW × 5 h = 0.5 kWh.

stem: A radioactive sample of 80 g has a half-life of 2 days. How much remains after 6 days?

explanationsWrong.A: 40 g is after only one half-life.
explanationsWrong.D: Decay halves each period; it doesn't divide the mass by 6.
